change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OAuth `state` is a constant, so it gives no CSRF protection
findings.body: `state = pipeline.signature` (line 402) is checked against `pipeline.signature` at line 412. `signature` is `md5(*view class names)` (`src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133`). It is the same for every user, session and attempt, and the test hard-codes it (`9cae5e88…`). Anyone can build a callback URL `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=9cae5e88…`. If a logged-in Sentry user opens it, their pipeline records the attacker's GitHub login as `github_authenticated_user`. That is a login-CSRF. The new check exists to prove the person completing the install is the GitHub user who installed the app, so the `state` should bind the callback to this browser session. The generic `OAuth2LoginView` uses `secrets.token_hex()`, stores it with `pipeline.bind_state("state", state)` and compares it in the callback (`src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:245-252`). Do the same here: generate a random state, bind it, and compare it with `request.GET.get('state')` at line 412 (ideally with `constant_time_compare`).

findings.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError for integrations without a stored sender
findings.body: `sender` is only written to metadata when the install webhook supplied it (`build_integration`, line 376-377, called from `InstallationEventWebhook` in `webhook.py:202-210`). Integrations created through the pipeline, or before this field existed, have no `sender`. `GitHubIntegrationsInstallationEndpoint` guards for this (`installation.py:44`). This branch is reached when an active `Integration` row exists with no `OrganizationIntegration`, which is the case the comment at line 492 describes, for example after an org removed the integration. For such a row line 501-504 raises `KeyError` and the user gets a 500 instead of the failure dialog. Use `integration.metadata.get('sender', {}).get('login')`, and decide explicitly what to do when it is missing. Do not let `None != None` pass silently if `github_authenticated_user` is also unset.

findings.title: Token exchange and user lookup can raise and return a 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` (line 423) is outside the `try`, and `get_user_info` (line 434) calls `raise_for_status()` (`src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16`). A connection error, SSL error, timeout, or a rejected token therefore surfaces as an unhandled exception, not the `error()` dialog used for the other failures here. The sibling `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token` catches `SSLError` and `ConnectionError` and returns an error payload (`src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:286-308`). Wrap both calls and return `error(...)`. The `error=access_denied` redirect GitHub sends when the user cancels is handled only by accident, because `code` is `None` and the exchange then fails.

findings.title: Authorize URL built by string interpolation without URL-encoding
findings.body: `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated raw into the query string. `OAuth2LoginView` uses `urlencode(params)` (`src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:250`). The `redirect_uri` is currently safe only because it has no query characters. Use `urlencode` so a future change to the URL or state does not break it. The test asserts the raw `redirect_uri=http://testserver/...` form, so it would need updating.

findings.title: Ownership check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: When no `Integration` exists for the `installation_id`, `GitHubInstallation` goes straight to `next_step()` (line 481-482) and the GitHub-user check at lines 500-505 never runs. Is that intended? The `Integration` row is created by the installation webhook, which can arrive after the user is redirected back to Sentry. In that window, or if the webhook is missed, the pipeline proceeds with a caller-supplied `installation_id` and no check of who owns it. `build_integration` then has no `sender` to compare against.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body: The second request sends `state=ddd023d8…`, which differs from the pipeline signature. The view returns `error(...)` at line 412-413 before any call to `/app/installations/...`, so the 404 stub at line 381-383 is never reached. The assertion was changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request.", so the test now checks a state mismatch. Coverage of the `IntegrationError` path in `build_integration` (integration.py:355-356) is gone. Either use the valid state and keep the original assertion, or rename the test to something like `test_invalid_state` and keep a separate not-found test.

findings.title: Missing coverage for the new OAuth view and the sender check's success and edge paths
findings.body: `test_github_user_mismatch` covers only the case where the sender differs. There is no test for the case where an existing Integration has `sender.login == 'octocat'`, no OrganizationIntegration, and the install succeeds. There is none for an Integration without a `sender` (the KeyError at integration.py:503). There is none for a failed token exchange (no `access_token`), a `/user` response without `login`, or a non-ACTIVE Integration hitting line 497-498. These are the new security-relevant branches.

contracts.action: New first pipeline step OAuthLoginView redirects to GitHub OAuth authorize, then handles the callback by exchanging the code and fetching the GitHub user
contracts.before_after: The generic views bind a random `state` in the session, bind `subdomain`, and `exchange_token` catches SSLError and ConnectionError (oauth2.py:245-256, 282-308). The new view uses the constant `pipeline.signature` as state, does not bind a state or subdomain, and does not catch network errors. It binds `installation_id` before validating state.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is bounced through GitHub authorize before the app-install page. A failure renders github-integration-failed.html via error() with 'Invalid installation request.'
contracts.failure_mode: State is not session-bound (finding at line 402). safe_urlopen and get_user_info exceptions propagate as a 500 (finding at line 423).

contracts.action: GitHubInstallation now compares the OAuth-authenticated GitHub login with integration.metadata['sender']['login'] when an Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration
contracts.before_after: The installation endpoint checks `'sender' not in integration.metadata` and returns 404 (installation.py:44-45). The new check indexes `metadata['sender']['login']` directly.
contracts.visible_effect: A matching user continues the pipeline. Otherwise the failure dialog is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: KeyError and a 500 when metadata has no sender (finding at line 503).

contracts.action: Inline FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR check in PipelineAdvancerView replaced by provider_id == 'github'
contracts.before_after: The behavior is the same, and the constant has no other references in the repository.

summary: The change adds a GitHub OAuth step so the installing GitHub user can be compared with the installation's `sender`. It has two defects. The OAuth `state` is the constant `pipeline.signature`, an md5 of the view class names, so it gives no CSRF protection. The sender check does `metadata[\"sender\"][\"login\"]` with no guard, which raises KeyError for integrations that have no stored sender. The token exchange and user lookup can also raise a 500 on network or HTTP errors. In the tests, `test_installation_not_found` now hits the state-mismatch branch and never reaches the installation lookup. The success path and edge branches of the sender check are untested. The `pipeline_advancer.py` change is a no-op refactor. I only read the code and did not run the tests.
